newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chubais to present spending cuts to Duma April 23.
newsitem.headline: Chubais to present spending cuts to Duma April 23.

text.p: Russian Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais will present a bill on spending cuts to the State Duma lower house of parliament on April 23, a senior member of the Duma budget committee said on Wednesday.
Oksana Dmitriyeva, deputy chairman of the budget committee, told Reuters the government would give an account to the Duma of how the 1997 budget was implemented in the first quarter.
The house had invited Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin to appear, but Dmitriyeva said Chubais, also first deputy prime minister, would probably address it.

Dmitriyeva said the Duma had not yet received data on the first quarter budget. But, according to unofficial information, revenues were 46-47 percent of budgeted levels while spending was 56 percent of planned levels.
Officials and other deputies have estimated first quarter tax receipts at 60 percent of budgeted levels.
According to the 1997 budget law, if revenues are more than 10 percent below plan, the government must present proposals to sequester, or cut, spending for the rest of the year.
Many categories of spending are protected, so that the cuts, in proportion to the shortfall in revenues, fall on only part of expenditure.
